az_sven_slab.blurb: A smooth granite slab on the north side of the McDowell Mountains, a short walk from the Tom's Thumb trailhead. The climbing is mostly trad, with a handful of bolted lines and top-rope options, and it asks for careful footwork: friction and small edges on fine granite crystals rather than big holds. Grades run from beginner-friendly up through the 5.10s and into 5.11 and 5.12, so there is something for most parties. One for the Road is a popular moderate. Cool months are the comfortable ones here, and the maze of side paths on the way in is easy to get lost in.
az_sven_slab.parking_note: Use the easternmost, main lot at the Tom's Thumb trailhead, at the end of 128th Street on the north side of the range.
az_sven_slab.approach: Head east on the Marcus Landslide trail for roughly a third of a mile, then turn right at the Sven Slab sign. Loop around a big boulder and over a low rise, then pick up the climbers' path on the right toward the Nit Nat flake. Many informal tracks dead-end in brush; if you are squeezing through thick scrub, turn back.

az_solitude_wall.blurb: A steep sport wall in Solitude Canyon on the west side of Mt. Elden above Flagstaff, climbed on sharp, grippy dacite. Most of the routes are bolted, with a few trad lines and a couple of boulder problems, and the grades are on the hard side: the bulk sit around 5.12 with a good number at 5.11 and 5.13. Expect dihedrals and aretes that finish with boulder-style cruxes, demanding crimps and body tension. Free Radical and Modest Mouse are among the standouts. The rock can be loose low on a route and cleaner higher up. Fall and spring are the easy seasons for it.
az_solitude_wall.approach: From the cul-de-sac, follow the wide trails up past the boulders, bear left into the canyon mouth, and keep going for about a quarter hour until a climbers' trail forks right near a gray sawn-off stump. It leads to the foot of the wall.

az_main_wall_center.blurb: The central section of the Main Wall in Isolation Canyon, a quartzite canyon cut by Pine Creek just south of the town of Pine. The rock is hard and covered in lichen, with good edges and more friction than it first looks like, and the routes are a mix of trad and bolted lines, often running a few pitches. Most of the grades fall between 5.9 and 5.12, with 5.10 and 5.11 the most common. Peacenik and Vitamin M are two of the better-known sport lines. Bring a standard trad rack and some long slings for linking pitches.
az_main_wall_center.parking_note: Drive south from Pine on Highway 87 to the paved Pine trailhead lot, which serves the Arizona Trail.
az_main_wall_center.approach: Follow the Arizona Trail southwest and downhill from the lot, pass the gate and ranch, then take the climbers' trail that branches left at the foot of the hill. Near Pine Creek, take the steep path up the creek's southern bank, cross the flat hilltop, and drop down to the walls.

az_ruins_the.blurb: A south-facing crag low on the Catalina Highway above Tucson, set among saguaros in the Sonoran Desert foothills of Mt. Lemmon. The climbing is mostly bolted, with some trad, and it concentrates heavily in the 5.10s, with a good number at 5.11 and only a few easier or harder lines. Black Feather and The Big Pow Wow are good 5.10c sport lines, and Before Limitations is a step up at 5.11c. Some routes need two ropes. The crag has a nice view down the mountain and makes a good winter outing.
az_ruins_the.parking_note: Pull into the lot at mile marker 4.7 on the Catalina Highway.
az_ruins_the.approach: Take the steep trail at the north end of the lot along the east ridge, go through the fence, and continue down to the base of the rock.

az_point_of_rocks.blurb: A cluster of granite towers, slots and a ridgeline of spires in the Granite Dells north of Prescott, reached from the Peavine Trail. The climbing is almost all trad, with a few bolted lines and a top rope or two, and it has an adventurous, exploratory feel: scrambling through intersecting slots, climbing short towers, and linking spires along the ridge. Grades span the easy 5.5 range up to 5.12, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.11. The south face catches the sun while the west side is shaded.
az_point_of_rocks.parking_note: Park at the small pull-off on N Granite Gardens Dr (room for four or five cars), or leave a car behind Three Sisters Consignment, or start at the main Peavine trailhead in Prescott and walk or bike.
az_point_of_rocks.approach: From the Granite Gardens pull-off, a short foot trail from the east side joins the Peavine Trail; Point of Rocks sits just north of the Storm Ranch area. A bicycle makes the approach quick from the other trailheads.

az_mormon_canyon.blurb: A remote sandstone canyon north of Sedona with long, serious trad routes, many of them three to nine pitches. Almost everything here is trad, spread over grades from about 5.7 to 5.12, with 5.10 through 5.12 making up most of it. Touched By An Angel is a long 5.10 outing, Spirit Compass is a four-pitch 5.12-, and Drinking Kool-Aid is another hard 5.12. Plan for a committing day: the walk in is long and brushy, the rock is soft and variable, and Sedona sandstone is easily damaged when it is wet.
az_mormon_canyon.parking_note: Leave Highway 89A on Jordan Road, turn left at the T, and follow the forest access signs along the dirt road to the lot at its end.
az_mormon_canyon.approach: From the lot, drop into the drainage on the right, turn left, and hike up the wash. Allow an hour to an hour and a half.

az_mouse_wall_the.blurb: A limestone sport wall in The Homestead, a remote desert canyon of single-pitch bolted climbs in Gila County, off Highway 77 between Globe and Winkelman. The Mouse Wall is nearly all sport, with grades from 5.7 up to 5.11 and the most routes around 5.9 and 5.10. Red Hot Rodent and Well Hung Minnie are two of the better lines. Bring a long rope and a rack of quickdraws, and carry water: the canyon is quiet and well away from services.
az_mouse_wall_the.parking_note: Turn off Highway 77 near mile marker 153 onto the primitive road, which runs about two miles to the Access Fund trailhead and camping area. A high-clearance, four-wheel-drive vehicle is advised for the rough stretch.
az_mouse_wall_the.approach: Walk the trail from the trailhead for about half a mile, then another few hundred yards to the canyon trails; the Mouse Wall can be reached from either branch at the fork.

az_avalon.blurb: A high-elevation crag near the top of Mt. Lemmon, within the Summit Crags, with mostly slab climbing on good rock and the occasional steep bulge. Sport and trad routes are mixed, and the grades lean moderate: lots of 5.8 to 5.10 with some easier and a few at 5.11 and 5.12. Little Miss Treatment is a 5.9 trad classic here. The face looks south, so it takes sun, while the trees at the base keep the ground shaded and make summer days pleasant. Twelve to fifteen quickdraws plus a light rack covers it. Afternoon storms can build.
az_avalon.parking_note: Drive to the top of the mountain and use the gravel parking on your left, a little short of the observatory.
az_avalon.approach: Follow the route toward Rappel Rock. At the saddle in front of it, skip the left-hand descent, take the good trail to the right, and stay close to the rock to reach the climbs.

az_glitter_box_area.blurb: A set of walls in Lower Devil's Canyon in Queen Creek Canyon, east of Phoenix, with a mix of bolted and gear-protected routes. Most of the climbing is 5.8 to 5.11, and 5.10 is the most common grade, so it suits a party looking for moderate to mid-grade routes. Eyes of the World is a 5.11a sport line, with Adios Larry, Gold and Damsel's Arete good 5.10s to try. The canyon sees fewer climbers than much of Queen Creek, partly because the road in is rough.
az_glitter_box_area.parking_note: Drive the dirt road in from Magma Mine Road to the end of the track if you have high-clearance four-wheel drive; otherwise pull off wherever the road feels comfortable and walk the last stretch, which is the roughest part.
az_glitter_box_area.approach: From the road's end, go through the gap in the barbed wire fence heading east. A climbers' trail branches left (north) toward the Glitter Box and another goes right toward the Totem Pole.

az_ultimates_east.blurb: The east side of the Ultimates in Upper Pumphouse Wash, a sandstone side canyon of Oak Creek Canyon just south of Flagstaff, with traditional lines up to 5.12+, a few newer sport routes and an offwidth. Most of the climbs are 5.10 through 5.12 and trad. Ultimate Dihedral and The Lorax are well-known crack and corner lines, and Pony Express is a popular sport route. Most routes on this side stay shaded for at least the first half of the day, and the plunge pools in the wash are a draw in summer. Getting in involves a short walk or rappels.
az_ultimates_east.parking_note: Exit I-17 at Newman Park Road, go west about 2.5 miles, then turn right onto forest road 253G for 0.8 mile to the parking spot.
